title: Bank of England Bank Rate decision, MPC Summary and minutes AND the February Monetary Policy Report (12:00 London / 07:00 ET) — the first forecast round of 2027
source: EST: bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the Bank's own upcoming-MPC-dates page lists 'Thursday 4 February' among its 2027 dates, marked PROVISIONAL, and describes the publication set verbatim as 'February MPC Summary and minutes and February Monetary Policy Report'. The same page lists 2026's remaining rounds as confirmed — 17 September (summary and minutes only), 5 November (summary, minutes AND the November Monetary Policy Report) and 17 December (summary and minutes only) — which is the contrast that makes the 2027 entries' provisional marking meaningful rather than boilerplate. Filed estimate on TWO independent counts, not one: the Bank itself calls the date provisional, and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the Bank of England in any case. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-labour-market-2027-01-19, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 LANE, 2026-09-09. WHY IT EARNS A SLOT: it is a genuine gap, not a refinement. This calendar carries boe-decision entries for 2026-12-17, 2027-04-29, 2027-06-17 and 2027-11-04 and NONE for 2027-02-04 — so the Bank's FIRST forecast round of 2027 is missing while two later 2027 rounds are present. It is also the single event the proposing print most directly feeds: uk-labour-market-2027-01-19 lands D-16, and the next labour print after it is 2027-02-16 ('16 February 2027 at 7:00am (confirmed)', gov.uk statistics-announcements register fetched 2026-09-09), twelve days AFTER this round. That makes the January print unambiguously the last labour read this committee sees before it publishes a full forecast — a placement established by register rather than, as the 12-15 sibling had to do for its own D-2 print, by argued precedent. WHY MEDIUM RATHER THAN LOW, and it is argued not copied: the sibling boe-decision-2026-12-17 and boe-decision-2027-04-29 entries are the comparison class, and a Monetary Policy Report round publishes a full conditioning forecast rather than summary, minutes and votes alone. The Report is also what should retire this chain's standing wage-anchor problem: the July 2026 MPR publishes a private-sector AWE path of 2.8% in 2026 Q2 and around 3.0% in Q3 and then stops, and no 2026 Q4 path is published anywhere findable on 2026-09-09 (re-checked today) — the 2026-11-05 Report is the near anchor and this one is the next. NO SYMBOLS AND NO PLAY: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol and no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed; the only channel is global term premium and it is second-order. PROMOTION CRITERION: the Bank moving this date from provisional to confirmed on its own upcoming-dates page, which is also the observation that would let a later lane raise the source prefix. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
